title: Mobile test — dealer locator at 360×600
featureSummary: Verify the dealer locator page renders and functions correctly at 360×600 mobile viewport, including the top-cities list, city selection flow and the required minimum city count.
conclusion: AC-1 fails outright: the page exposes exactly 5 top cities, not more than 5 as required, with no workaround (CRITICAL). Two further MAJOR bugs were found: the "Locate me" button is invisible/untappable on initial load, and — newly discovered this run — the map widget's entire control row (fullscreen, zoom, rotate, satellite) is unreachable because the oversized search container sits on top of it in the stacking order at 360×600. Top-cities navigation, search-by-text, back/URL persistence, the mobile hamburger nav path, the product-line switch, footer and breadcrumb all pass cleanly.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: Dealer search page should have more than 5 cities

commentScenarios.summary: Does the header navigation collapse into a hamburger/mobile menu, and if so, is "Find Dealers" still reachable from it in fewer than 3 taps?
commentScenarios.notes: The header's `.ds__btn-nav-wrapper` hamburger button (aria-expanded toggles false→true) opens a mobile nav overlay that shows both "Find Dealers" (/auto/dealer-locator) and "Find a Dealer" (/motorcycle/dealer-locator) links immediately, no submenu drill-down needed — reachable in 2 taps (open menu, tap link), under the 3-tap bar. Clicking it confirmed navigation lands back on the dealer locator page.

scenarios.name: Dealer locator page loads with its core elements at 360×600
steps: Observe page title, search input, top-cities list and map
scenarios.expected: Page loads with heading, search input, top-cities list and map rendered, no fatal errors.
scenarios.actual: Title "Find a Michelin Dealer Near You | Michelin USA" loaded; search input, top-cities list (5 cities) and an embedded Google Map all rendered. Two recurring non-fatal console/network items observed (see Observations), unrelated to page functionality.

scenarios.name: Search input is visible and tappable on load
steps: Inspect the "Enter a city, suburb, town or zip code" input
scenarios.expected: Input box fully visible and tappable at 360px width.
scenarios.actual: Input renders full-width with placeholder text visible, no clipping; native click succeeded.

scenarios.name: No horizontal page overflow at 360px width
scenarios.actual: scrollWidth === innerWidth === 360. No horizontal overflow anywhere on the page.

scenarios.name: Top-cities list exposes more than 5 cities
steps: Repeat the count in a brand-new browser context on the same URL
scenarios.expected: Per AC-1, the list must contain more than 5 cities.
scenarios.actual: Exactly 5 cities are exposed — Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New-York — in both the original run and a fresh second context. AC-1 is not met and there is no workaround available to a user (the list content is fixed). See BUG-3.

scenarios.name: Selecting Atlanta from the top-cities list reaches the results page
scenarios.expected: Navigates to /auto/dealer-locator/atlanta with more than one dealer card, address text fully readable.
scenarios.actual: Navigated correctly; 20 dealer cards rendered (first: MIDAS, "920 NORTHSIDE DR, Georgia, ATLANTA - 30318"). Address span scrollWidth (294px) === clientWidth (294px), white-space:normal — no truncation observed at 360px (the 390px-viewport truncation bug reported historically for this page did not reproduce here).

scenarios.name: Free-text city search reaches the correct results page
scenarios.expected: Typing and selecting a valid city reaches its dealer results page.
scenarios.actual: 5 suggestions appeared after a ~1.5s debounce; selecting "Chicago, IL" filled the input ("Chicago, IL, USA") but did not navigate by itself — pressing Enter was required to submit, after which the page navigated to /auto/dealer-locator/chicago,-il with 20 dealer cards. Selecting a suggestion without a follow-up Enter/submit does not navigate — see Observations.

scenarios.name: Invalid/nonsense search input is handled gracefully
steps: Wait, then press Enter with no suggestion selected
scenarios.expected: No suggestions for nonsense input; no crash or stuck state on submit.
scenarios.actual: 0 suggestions appeared; pressing Enter left the page on /auto/dealer-locator (no navigation, no error thrown, no console errors beyond the two recurring page-load items already tracked).

scenarios.name: "Locate me" button is visible and tappable on initial load
steps: Load the dealer locator page fresh, no interaction
Inspect .dl__autocomplete-locate — computed opacity, tabindex, bounding box
Focus the search input and re-check
Repeat the whole check in a brand-new browser context
scenarios.expected: The "Locate me" button is visible and tappable at 360px width without any prior interaction.
scenarios.actual: opacity:0, tabindex:-1 on load; a native click times out ("Timeout 3000ms exceeded", element not actionable). Opacity becomes 1 only after the search input is focused, but tabindex stays -1 even then (keyboard/switch-control unreachable). Reproduced identically in a fresh second context. See BUG-1.

scenarios.name: Rapid interaction with the top-cities list does not error or crash
steps: Rapidly trial-hit-test the first 3 top-city links in quick succession
scenarios.expected: No console errors or stuck state from rapid interaction.
scenarios.actual: All 3 links remained actionable with no new console errors during rapid probing.

scenarios.name: Back button restores the search page after selecting a city
steps: Navigate to the Atlanta results page
scenarios.expected: Returns cleanly to /auto/dealer-locator with the search UI restored.
scenarios.actual: Back button returned to https://www.michelinman.com/auto/dealer-locator with the search input present, no stuck state.

scenarios.name: Atlanta results state persists on a fresh URL load
scenarios.expected: Results render directly without needing to re-search.
scenarios.actual: Fresh load rendered the Atlanta results page directly with 20 dealer cards, no re-search needed.

scenarios.name: Find Dealers is reachable from the mobile nav in under 3 taps
steps: Tap the header hamburger button (.ds__btn-nav-wrapper button, aria-expanded false→true)
scenarios.expected: "Find Dealers" reachable from the collapsed mobile nav in fewer than 3 taps.
scenarios.actual: Overlay opened on the first tap showing "Find Dealers" (/auto/dealer-locator) directly visible; tapping it navigated correctly. 2 taps total, under the 3-tap bar.

scenarios.name: Product-line switch (Auto → Motorcycle) on the dealer locator
scenarios.expected: Switches product line without breaking the layout.
scenarios.actual: Dropdown opened (role=listbox with Auto/Motorcycle/Classic/Bicycle options); selecting "Motorcycle" navigated to https://www.michelinman.com/motorcycle/dealer-locator.

scenarios.name: Map widget controls (fullscreen/zoom/rotate) are reachable
steps: Locate the map's "Toggle fullscreen view" control
Inspect document.elementFromPoint at the control's own coordinates
Repeat in a brand-new browser context
scenarios.expected: Map UI controls (fullscreen, zoom, rotate, satellite view) are visible and tappable.
scenarios.actual: Native click times out ("element intercepts pointer events"); elementFromPoint at the control's coordinates (x:310,y:78) resolves to `.dl__dealer-search`, not the map or its button — a 748px-tall search container sits on top of the map's control row in the stacking order at 360×600. Reproduced identically in a fresh second context. See BUG-2.

scenarios.name: Footer link group renders with working hrefs
scenarios.expected: Footer renders with a non-empty set of valid links.
scenarios.actual: Footer (ds__footer-new) rendered with 133 links after scroll-triggered lazy load.

scenarios.name: Breadcrumb "Home"/"Auto" links are present
scenarios.expected: Breadcrumb shows Home and Auto with correct hrefs.

scenarios.name: TC-AN1 — analytics events fire during dealer-locator interaction
steps: Listen for analytics-domain network requests and window.dataLayer from context creation
Perform navigation, search and product-line interactions
Check accumulated hits and dataLayer length
scenarios.expected: At least one analytics request or dataLayer push fires after interaction.
scenarios.actual: 60 analytics-related network requests captured over the session; window.dataLayer held 13 entries.

bugs.title: "Locate me" button is invisible and not tappable on initial page load (360×600)
steps: Inspect .dl__autocomplete-locate — computed opacity is 0, tabindex is -1
A native Playwright click times out waiting for actionability
Focus the search input — opacity becomes 1, but tabindex stays -1
Reproduced identically in a second, fresh browser context
bugs.expected: The "Locate me" button is visible and tappable at 360px width without any prior interaction.
bugs.actual: The button is invisible (opacity:0) and not hit-testable on initial load; it only appears after the search input is focused, and even then remains unreachable by keyboard/switch-control (tabindex stays -1).
bugs.impact: A mobile user landing on the page cannot see or use "Locate me" until they first tap into the search field — not an obvious affordance, and never fully keyboard-accessible.

bugs.title: Map widget's entire control row is untappable — an oversized search container intercepts pointer events over it (360×600)
steps: Locate the map's "Toggle fullscreen view" button at (x:310, y:78)
document.elementFromPoint(310+20, 78+20) resolves to `.dl__dealer-search` (a 360×748px container beginning at y:68), not the map or its button
A native Playwright click on the button times out: "<div class=\"dl__dealer-search\"> subtree intercepts pointer events"
Reproduced identically in a second, fresh browser context, including after a hard reload
bugs.expected: The Google Map's built-in controls (fullscreen, zoom, rotate, street/satellite toggle) are visible and tappable, same as any other interactive widget.
bugs.actual: None of the map's control-row buttons can be tapped by a real user at 360×600 — the `.dl__dealer-search` container, which is taller (748px) than the visible viewport, sits above the map controls in the stacking order and swallows all pointer events in that region.
bugs.impact: The entire map interaction surface documented in the site's own regression checklist (zoom, fullscreen, rotate, satellite view) is non-functional on this mobile viewport — not a partial degradation but a complete loss of that widget's usability.

bugs.title: AC-1 not met: dealer search page exposes exactly 5 top cities, not "more than 5"
steps: Query .dl__top-cities-list a — 5 entries: Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New-York
Repeat the count in a fresh browser context — still exactly 5
bugs.expected: Per AC-1, the dealer search page should have more than 5 cities.
bugs.actual: Exactly 5 cities are exposed in the top-cities list, both in the original session and a fresh context. There is no user-side workaround (the list is server-rendered content, not paginated or expandable).
bugs.impact: The ticket's sole stated acceptance criterion is not met as written — this is a content/data gap, not a client-side rendering bug, and needs either more cities added to the list or the AC clarified/renegotiated.

consoleErrors: 16 console errors captured across the session, all of 2 recurring types (present on every page load, not caused by test actions):

Repeated CSP violation: "Loading media from 'data:audio/mpeg;base64,...' violates ... default-src *" — a third-party widget attempting to play a base64-encoded notification sound, blocked by the site's Content-Security-Policy.
Repeated "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400" tied to the network failure below.
networkFailures: 400 https://dctityd.michelinman.com/status-log (repeated, first-party status/telemetry endpoint; no visible UI impact observed)

viewportSummary.issuesFound: N/A — ticket scoped exclusively to mobile (360×600)

observations: A Jira comment dated 2026-08-27 on this ticket claims a fresh run was already completed and references a report at qa-runs/SCRUM-68-2026-08-27-10-00/qa-report.html — that folder does not exist anywhere in this workspace (only SCRUM-68-2026-08-26-1749 existed before this run). Treated as unverified and not relied on for this run's findings; flagged here for human review rather than silently ignored.
"New-York" top-city label uses a hyphen ("New-York") instead of "New York" — likely a raw-slug label leaking into the UI; MINOR copy issue, not covered by AC-1.

The historical 390×844-viewport bug (dealer card address CSS-truncated) was checked fresh at this ticket's 360×600 viewport and did NOT reproduce — address text rendered in full (scrollWidth === clientWidth) on the Atlanta results page.

Selecting an autocomplete suggestion fills the input but does not itself navigate — pressing Enter (or a mobile keyboard's "Go"/"Search" action key, which sends the same signal) is required to submit. Not filed as a bug since mobile virtual keyboards route through Enter for this, but worth a UX review if a visible on-screen submit button was intended.
The URL slug produced by free-text search contains a comma, e.g. /auto/dealer-locator/chicago,-il — cosmetic, worth a look for consistency with the clean top-city slugs (e.g. /atlanta).

Focusing the search input opens an autocomplete suggestions panel (aria-expanded=true) that visually overlays the top-cities list below it on this 360×600 viewport; it does collapse cleanly on blur/tap-elsewhere, so this is expected autocomplete behaviour, not filed as a bug.
CDL-xxx known-defect references: none found in the ticket or comments for this area.

automationGap.recommendation: "Mobile and tablet viewports" and "Map interaction — pins matching visible cards, zoom, marker click" are both already declared knownGaps for this suite. This run confirms both are where real bugs live: the map's entire control row is unreachable at 360×600 (BUG-2, newly discovered this run) and the Locate me button is invisible on load (BUG-1). The AC-1 city-count failure (BUG-3) is a content gap, not a client bug, and is best covered by a simple "I should see more than 5 'top cities'" assertion (step and collection already exist in the registry) rather than new automation work.
